artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
12 Things I Forgot" is a single by Steven Wilson released in November 2020 as part of the promotional campaign leading up to his sixth studio album, The Future Bites. The track exemplifies Wilson's expanded exploration of electronic and dance-oriented production that would define the full album's sonic direction. Released ahead of the album's January 2021 debut, "12 Things I Forgot" served as an early indicator of Wilson's shift toward more accessible, rhythmically-driven material while maintaining the artistic depth characteristic of his work.

The single blends electronic, rock, and pop elements, positioning itself within Wilson's broader artistic evolution during this period. Co-produced by Wilson and David Kosten, the track demonstrates the collaborative approach that shaped The Future Bites, which dealt thematically with identity and technology in contemporary society. The limited edition physical release included additional tracks such as "Move Like a Fever" and "King Ghost," offering listeners extended material beyond the single's core composition.

As part of the The Future Bites era, "12 Things I Forgot" reflected Wilson's willingness to experiment with dance and neo-disco influences while preserving a rock sensibility—a balance that defined the album's critical reception as a curious, contemporary examination of modern life rather than a dystopian warning. The single's release strategy underscored Wilson's continued engagement with both digital and physical formats, appealing to his established progressive rock audience while reaching toward broader electronic and pop listeners.
